data.name: Jaladhar
data.gender_notes: Jaladhar is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Jaladhar means the one who holds or mover of water. It is derived from the Sanskrit words Jala (water) and Dhara (holder or bearer). This name is associated with the god Varuna, who is the god of water, oceans and rivers. The name Jaladhar carries the meaning “Mover of water” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Jaladhar usually hope their child will grow to embody mover of water and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Jaladhar represents the divine power of water and its ability to nourish and sustain life. It also symbolizes the strength and stability of the one who holds or moves the water, signifying power and prosperity.
data.etymology: Jaladhar belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Mover of water.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jaladhar total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

Hindu scriptures like the Rig Veda credit various gods with the creation of water. This name signals a deep connection to water and the natural elements, which is a significant aspect of Hindu tradition and spirituality.
